supplementary.classification_reason: Additional synthesis in the original 2023 annual volume; retained as an unaltered supplementary treatment.

introduction.title: Mathematics Atlas · 2023–21 October 2026
introduction.subtitle: A domain synthesis, complete treatment catalogue, and ten interactive worked models
introduction.scope: This atlas unifies the four completed retrospective mathematics volumes: 114 treatments for 2023, 237 for 2024, 351 for 2025 and 349 for 2026, for a total of 1,051 main treatments. Fourteen additional 2023 synthesis treatments are retained separately, giving 1,065 retained treatment bodies including supplements. These are treatments, not a count of unique conversations or distinct mathematical ideas. The source boundary is the four retrieved annual bundles, not a fresh complete export of every account conversation. The 2026 boundary is 21 October 2026; no later month is inferred. Historical dates identify the dated topics; revised proofs and examples are retrospective exposition and must not be read as discoveries made on those historical dates.
introduction.method: The chronological volumes remain intact. Above them, this report groups related material into domain chapters and canonical concept families. A family gives precise objects, a scoped theorem, a proof, a worked example, limits and concrete next questions. Its source identifiers allow the reader to return to every original treatment. Domain assignment is an editorial navigation aid, with secondary links for real cross-domain content; it is not an assertion that mathematical subjects have disjoint boundaries. Repeated annual treatments may support one family, and one treatment may support several families.
introduction.argument: The most productive organizing principle is a sequence of obligations: specify the object and admissible maps, identify the target, state hypotheses, derive a result, compute a checkable example, and expose what remains unresolved. Quotients ask which distinctions matter; cohomology asks whether local data glue; spectra quantify suppression and amplification; counting turns finite configuration spaces into exact laws and certificates; deformation tests whether a leading-order structure survives higher compatibility conditions; arithmetic reduction turns some infinite families into finite representative checks. These are connected through explicit constructions, not through a universal theory claimed to contain them all.
introduction.interactivity: The interactive companion has two different functions. Its catalogue provides search, domain/year/capability filters and the complete retained text of all 1,051 source treatments. Its ten labs implement small, explicitly specified mathematical models. A capability tag on a chapter means the mathematics supports that kind of operation; it does not mean a general solver for that domain has been implemented. Each lab identifies its inputs, arithmetic, output and limits. Exact rational or integer results are distinguished from floating evaluations, analytic upper bounds and conceptual research directions.
introduction.reading: Read the domain overview to orient the objects and questions, then a concept family for its theorem and proof. Follow a source identifier to inspect the original revised question and treatment. Use a lab to vary parameters inside a stated model. Use a cross-domain bridge only with its displayed hypotheses. The report is deliberately not another concatenation of the annual volumes: the full source bodies are retained in the interactive catalogue and portable bundle, while this document develops the shared architecture and the strongest concept families in depth.
introduction.verification: The four original annual verification suites were replayed successfully from fresh copies. They contain 61 verifier programs and 1,173 scoped records; records are heterogeneous and include a proof-only record, so these counts are not counts of formally proved theorems. New domain scripts check selected worked examples, and the lab engine is tested against independent exact fixtures and boundary cases. A passing finite check supports its named model and does not automatically certify an entire exposition or an unrecovered historical instance.

chapters.title: Arithmetic and number fields
chapters.organizing_question: How can an exact arithmetic construction retain its scalar domain, local data and completeness certificate as it is transported into a larger mathematical framework?
core_objects: Integer valuation vectors and divisor incidence
p-adic fields, residue systems and integral series
Quadratic units and complete Pell orbits
Cyclotomic fields and finite Galois fibres
Ideal classes, norm lattices and ramification
Modular coefficients, local factors and convergent Dirichlet series
chapters.overview:
The strongest arithmetic thread across the recovered treatments is the replacement of suggestive numerical association with a declared object and a certificate. A number such as 384 becomes useful after it is assigned to the degree of a cyclotomic field. A recurrence becomes a classification after descent proves every solution lies in its seed orbits. A polynomial becomes an arithmetic field description after irreducibility, discriminant and ramification are checked. A residue becomes a root certificate after compatibility, a unit derivative and completeness supply the infinite conclusion. These transitions are the organizing structure of this chapter.

The entry point is scalar type. The 2023 distinction between Q, Q_p and characteristic-p series rings prevents invalid maps before any calculation begins. The same issue returns in finite-precision Frobenius tests and formal-series invariants: zero modulo p^N can hide a nonzero obstruction, and an unknown tail can hide the first unit coefficient. The p-adic family therefore couples exact digits with a proof about the completed object. Valuation arithmetic then gives the complementary integer picture. Prime exponents turn monomial constraints into affine integer lattices, divisor order into a product of chains, and factorials into a p-power part plus a stripped unit. The gcd-matrix factorization demonstrates how such arithmetic can legitimately create an energy form through an explicit incidence map.

Two families support implemented finite interactive models. The conductor-1680 model enumerates 384 units, reduces them to eight primitive order-30 classes and verifies 48 points in every fibre. The tower formula then gives exact trace transport. The Pell model generates positive and negative norm orbits, displays inverse steps and computes periodic congruence acceptance. Its written seed reduction is essential: enumeration explains a finite modular period, while descent proves global coverage. Both labs are worked models with exact inputs and outputs, rather than general arithmetic-solving services.

Number fields provide the main obstruction language. The S₃ closure of the discriminant-minus-23 cubic forbids cyclotomic containment. The Q(√10) examples distinguish a genuine unramified class-field candidate from an extension of the right degree with the wrong ramification. Cubic norm formulas preserve the lattice defining the original binary equation, showing exactly why a unit action can leave the solution plane. The completely proved Mordell example y²=x³−2 illustrates the stronger standard: a norm-Euclidean ring and coprimality argument can deliver a global finite answer, whereas an ambient unit identity alone cannot.

The final two families connect this arithmetic to analytic and modular structure. Modular forms require a group, weight and normalization before dimensions and Hecke relations make sense. Euler products require a convergence half-plane before coefficient algebra becomes analysis. Pointwise μΛ, convolution μ*log, prime counting and prime-power counting remain different objects. These distinctions make cross-domain bridges more productive because each bridge names its actual map. The chapter does not force a chronological storyline where sources are absent: the conductor thread is supported in 2025–2026, the explicit Pell thread in 2024 and 2026, and the modular thread primarily in 2024–2025. The common framework is a new synthesis of those supported mathematical treatments.
chapters.open_frontier: The most valuable extensions would certify complete unit bases and lattice-return conditions for the norm examples, extend seed proofs to additional Pell cores, and provide explicit integral intertwiners for the proposed conductor-to-lattice bridge. Each is a precise missing theorem or certificate rather than an unspecified generalization.

chapters.title: Algebraic and arithmetic geometry
chapters.organizing_question: Which geometric model, maps and comparison data make a claim about arithmetic, singularities or cohomology precise enough to prove?
core_objects: Affine curves, normalizations and projective models
Divisors, line bundles and spaces of sections
Modular curves, cusps and toric boundary charts
Elliptic groups, Frobenius factors and height lattices
chapters.overview:
This domain is organized by the object to which a statement applies. An affine equation, its singular curve, the normalized function-field model and the smooth compact curve answer different questions. A point count, a rational group, a divisor class and a cohomology realization likewise retain different information. The best revision of the earlier questions is to specify that object first, then ask for a map or invariant with hypotheses that can be checked. This replaces a broad request for additional geometric structure with a sequence of concrete mathematical tasks.

The curve family begins with maps. Rational parametrization includes an exceptional point and an inverse domain. The cusp map t↦(t²,t³) is injective but has zero derivative at the origin; its normalization ring and local intersection multiplicity expose what a set-theoretic description misses. The 2026 corner cubic adds an exact birational coordinate change, while the superelliptic family computes genus only after finite and infinite ramification are counted on the smooth compact normalization. These examples provide reusable questions for any proposed parameter map: where is it defined, where does rank drop, what happens at infinity, and which inverse identity is actually proved?

Divisors and positivity organize the 2023 arithmetic-quotient cluster. Neatness addresses stabilizers in the open quotient; the cusp coordinate fills a puncture; a regular fan addresses local boundary smoothness; the canonical or log-canonical divisor addresses growth of sections; a very ample line bundle addresses an embedding. The modular curves X(3) and X(7) make ordinary and logarithmic general type visibly different. Riemann–Roch and Serre duality then give a precise degree threshold for a curve embedding. Picard calculations on P¹×P¹ and invariant divisor subspaces provide finite exact models of the same language. Higher-dimensional claims remain bounded by the actual compactification and positivity data supplied.

Elliptic arithmetic is the strongest local-to-global example. The discriminant-37 curve recurs in the 2024 and 2026 treatments with exact finite counts and rational group computations. Two good reductions exclude every possible rational torsion prime; the nonzero point then proves a rank lower bound. Heights turn independence into a Gram certificate, but a subgroup regulator differs by an index square from the full regulator. Selmer groups add hidden torsors and therefore supply information different from an explicit generator list. The interactive capacity here is specified as a recipe for exact point and group checks; no general certified rank or integral-point engine is claimed.

The cohomological family supplies a general caution about forgetting structure. An Euler realization can erase nonzero groups or take negative values. Rational monodromy ranks can erase integral torsion. A nilpotent operator determines a weight filtration but does not by itself produce a limiting mixed Hodge structure. Étale, crystalline, de Rham and Betti comparisons require compatible bases, coefficients and geometric hypotheses; a false universal motivic–Betti isomorphism already fails at a point. These are constructive constraints: they tell a future interface which fields and degrees to require and which counterexamples to expose. Together the four families form an atlas of models, maps and information loss, with each purported cross-domain identification stated as a theorem still requiring its own certificate.
chapters.open_frontier: The next substantial work would supply explicit global compactification data in a fixed higher-dimensional example, certified descent and saturation for the elliptic subgroup, and correctly graded functorial comparison maps. A numerical invariant can assist those tasks but cannot replace the relevant geometry or cohomology.

chapters.title: Algebra and representation theory: structures, actions and exact certificates
chapters.organizing_question: What algebraic structure is specified, and which exact maps or identities justify the invariant being claimed?
chapters.overview:
Algebra provides the atlas with a language for separating a structure from its numerical shadow. A carrier with a multiplication law is more information than a cardinality; a representation is more information than a dimension; a spectral decomposition is more information than an eigenvalue list. Across the source years, the strongest developments begin when the multiplication, action, field and equivalence relation become explicit. The six families in this domain organise those developments around operations, linear certificates, symmetry, bracket structure, finite local models and operator states.

Typed operations come first because they determine which equations even make sense. Transporting a field through a bijection produces a valid isomorphic field, while merely changing notation or mixing transported and ordinary operations does not. Capped counters create finite monoids with an absorbing top layer and a minimal multiplication ideal; they do not automatically create a vector-space nullspace. Ring quotients, maximal ideals and squarefree branch decompositions then show how discarded information is certified by an actual homomorphism. The finite cases are useful because every product and every ideal condition can be replayed.

Linear structure supplies a second layer of certificates. Rank needs both upper and lower witnesses, singular values need declared metrics, and projectors need their idempotent and annihilation equations. A squarefree annihilating polynomial yields a decomposition only after checking the polynomial identity, and every advertised spectral point still needs nonzero support. These distinctions connect algebra to observation and stability throughout the atlas. They also prevent exact rational rank, integral torsion and floating effective rank from being treated as the same quantity.

Symmetry becomes productive through actual actions. Finite averaging gives invariant projectors; orbit counts give stabilizers; characters and branching specify which modules occur. The B₄ action over F₃ has a complete Hamming-weight classification, while a signed-permutation invariant quadratic form must be scalar. Neither result forces an empirical dataset rank or a unique frequency ratio on a multiplicity space. Exceptional symmetry is retained at its honest level: the E₈ root accounting and 120+128 decomposition are exact, but an exceptional bracket needs equivariant maps and Jacobi beyond a dimension count. Octonions sharpen this lesson by providing a nonassociative product with a sharp, convention-sensitive defect theorem.

Finite local and path algebras add the geometry of relations. The four-dimensional jet algebra needs cubic closure; its symmetric Hilbert function coexists with a two-dimensional socle. The rank-thirteen quiver pencil has a global path-bundle proof of flatness, while its full Hochschild profile remains another calculation. Finally, faithful finite operator states supply modular flow and KMS identities in a setting where all formulas can be derived directly. These finite models connect outward to categories, geometry, quantum theory and inference through explicit maps. The domain therefore aims at inspectable structure and proof, with larger classification and infinite analytic problems stated as precise frontiers rather than inferred from familiar names.
core_objects: Octonion and graded brackets; exceptional roots
chapters.open_frontier: Recover the actual multiplication, representation and cochain matrices behind the larger historical objects; then test completeness of invariants, exceptional bracket identities and parameter-stratified derived invariants.

chapters.title: Categories and homological methods
chapters.organizing_question: Which constructions preserve the object, and what explicit maps certify preservation?
core_objects: resolutions, Tor, Ext and cotangent complexes
filtrations, page differentials and inverse systems
chapters.overview:
This domain supplies the architecture used to compose the rest of the atlas. Its organizing unit is a construction together with the equations that make it valid. A category needs a declared class of morphisms and a composition law; a dynamical intertwiner must commute with evolution. A quotient needs an equivalence relation; its universal factorization identifies exactly which maps survive the loss of distinctions. A pushout needs two arrows from shared data and produces one object encoding all compatible pairs of outgoing maps. These examples give a precise language for composing mathematics without treating a common label or equal dimension as a structural identification.

The next layer is homological. A complex is more than a sequence of vector spaces because its differential must square to zero. Signed totalization, shifts and cones make this requirement explicit across degrees. A chain contraction gives a finite certificate that a reduction preserves cohomology. Its homotopy exhibits the difference between the identity and a reduced reconstruction as a boundary correction. This is the appropriate bridge to smaller models: one may eliminate a contractible pair while preserving homology, even though total coordinate dimension changes. The chapter therefore separates presentation size, rank information and invariant content.

Derived constructions retain information that ordinary products and kernels erase. Tor and Ext arise by resolving an object before applying a nonexact functor. A nonzero extension class can distinguish modules with identical dimension; the size of the whole Ext group cannot decide whether one selected extension splits. Similarly a tangent complex supplies potential obstruction spaces, while the actual higher-order lifting equation determines an obstruction class. The double-point and finite Maurer–Cartan examples show both outcomes: a nonzero first-order direction can fail to lift, while a nonzero quadratic cocycle can be removable because it is a boundary. These are constructive alternatives with explicit witnesses.

Finally, filtered and infinite constructions state what remains unknown after a partial computation. The associated graded forgets how layers attach. Page differentials can kill apparent classes, and integral extensions can distinguish groups with identical limiting graded pieces. Inverse limits introduce genuinely infinite compatibility constraints that finite truncations do not settle. Perverse shifts, coefficient base change and t-structures belong in this same discipline of declared data: they change the interpretation of degrees and comparisons. The dated source continuity is strongest from the 2024 categorical and spectral questions through the 2025 derived examples to the 2026 exact signs, limits and obstruction calculations. Those dates locate topics in the available corpus; they do not date the creation of the new proofs here.

The interactive capacity is consequently a certificate interface. Finite matrices can test d²=0, construct a cone, verify a contraction and compare homology. They cannot manufacture the missing differential, functor or higher coherence map of an unspecified object. The chapter’s open frontier is to replace those absent operators with explicit constructions and then verify comparison maps at the correct coefficient and categorical level.
chapters.open_frontier: Build actual comparison functors, controlling complexes and higher-coherence maps for the proposed structures; compute unknown differentials and extension classes before claiming equivalence or reconstruction.

chapters.title: Topology, cohomology and gluing
chapters.organizing_question: Which global features survive local changes, and which exact obstruction prevents a global construction?
core_objects: spaces with declared cells and attachments
chapters.overview:
The topological domain is organized around two constructive tasks: calculate an invariant of a specified space, and identify an obstruction to assembling local information globally. The first begins with cells and boundaries. A graph, the surface on which it is drawn and a filling of its cycles are different spaces. Their boundary matrices make the distinction exact. A triangle boundary has a one-dimensional cycle; attaching its face kills that class. The same principle scales to flag complexes, polyhedral boundaries and singular links, where the problem is to state the actual attachment data before assigning a homology group.

Coefficients determine what the calculation can see. Rational Betti numbers retain free rank but erase torsion. Integer normal forms supply the finite abelian groups hidden by that compression, and reduction modulo a prime can reveal a different pattern again. Reduced homology and intersection homology refine different aspects of a space: one adjusts the degree-zero basepoint contribution, while the other controls allowable chains near specified singular strata. The contractible cone on a torus makes the latter concrete, because ordinary bounding disks may be disallowed at the apex. These distinctions improve classification questions by matching the invariant to the equivalence relation and phenomenon under study.

Persistence adds maps and time to this framework. It retains finite-lived classes that disappear in the eventual space. A legal filtration orders cells after their faces, and induced maps determine births and deaths. Small exact examples support a clear interactive model, while shifted sublevel inclusions give a direct perturbation certificate. Random entry times connect topological lifetimes to order statistics in the simple square example. The scope stays explicit: a stable barcode is a controlled invariant of the declared filtration, not a complete reconstruction of the geometry or a validation of the mechanism generating the data.

The local-to-global side starts with the sheaf axiom’s actual content: compatible data glue uniquely. Arbitrary discrepancies need not be compatible, and their failure can occupy a nonzero cohomology group. Incidence equations, cycle periods and rank-one transport give complete exact examples. Discrete Hodge theory chooses harmonic representatives after an inner product is declared; it does not make every harmonic vector a zero class. Consequently a small residual or a successful test vector cannot certify disappearance of an entire obstruction space. A comparison between local models needs a cochain equivalence if it is to preserve those classes.

Periods, group multipliers and characteristic classes connect this algebraic computation to geometric invariance. Rephasing changes a multiplier by a coboundary, nonvanishing loop homotopies preserve winding, and normalized bundle curvature represents characteristic classes. The family treatments keep their degrees and coefficients separate while exposing their shared local-choice versus global-defect mechanism. This makes the domain’s interactive capacity concrete: supply a finite complex or transport system, and return a cycle, a potential, a barcode or a nonzero obstruction certificate. The frontier is to recover missing attachment, coefficient and comparison data in larger historical proposals rather than infer topology from terminology.
chapters.open_frontier: Specify the spaces, coefficient systems, legal filtrations and attachment maps in the larger proposals; produce integer certificates and valid cochain comparisons that preserve the intended global obstruction.

chapters.title: Differential and symplectic geometry
chapters.organizing_question: What becomes computable once the metric, form, connection and symmetry are explicitly declared?
core_objects: moving frames, curvature functionals and geometric curves
chapters.overview:
This domain connects local geometric structure to calculable global behavior. The first input is a declared metric, differential form or connection. Coordinates alone supply none of these. Once a metric is given, one can derive length, geodesics, curvature, volume growth and spectral scaling; once a symplectic form and Hamiltonian are given, one can derive a vector field and test conservation. This order of construction turns the archive’s geometric vocabulary into a set of mathematical interfaces with explicit assumptions and outputs.

Metric geometry separates representation changes from genuine geometric deformation. The hyperbolic half-plane has computable Christoffel symbols, vertical unit-speed geodesics and curvature minus one. Its exponential volume growth prevents a global Euclidean doubling argument even though every smooth point is locally Euclidean in the appropriate sense. Constant scaling links length, curvature and spectral thresholds through exact powers. Discrete transport curvature and prefix ultrametrics then show how different metric inputs answer different questions: probability measures matter for Ollivier curvature, while digit carries obstruct the inverse inference from real distance to prefix agreement. Neither a positive weight table nor an unexplained singular value is a metric-independent invariant.

Symplectic and contact geometry organize mechanics and reduction. Conservation of one Hamiltonian does not make it a Casimir. Removing a cyclic coordinate is a legitimate reduction only at a fixed momentum level, where the restricted two-form’s null directions are precisely the symmetry directions being quotiented. A regular moment-map quotient can be identified with a cotangent bundle in explicit charts. The oscillator demonstrates another kind of geometric change: a generating function blows up at a projection caustic while the underlying phase-space trajectory remains smooth. A Legendrian curve and a thermodynamic potential similarly require the contact form and tangent condition before their consequences follow.

Connections supply transport, curvature measures local two-dimensional noncommutation, and holonomy records a global loop. A flat circle system can have nontrivial monodromy; a curved connection on the plane can live on a trivial bundle; a Berry eigenline over the sphere can obstruct a global smooth potential. The exact shear loop makes noncommutativity and gauge conjugacy visible in finite matrices. It is the appropriate worked model for the interactive atlas, with a clear gap between this calculation and an empirical connection whose actual matrices or two-dimensional refinement are unavailable.

Curves and variational geometry complete the domain by integrating local data into shapes. Frenet frames are rotation equations tied to regularity, moving affine frames introduce explicit derivative terms, and linear curvature uniquely minimizes one declared curvature-rate functional. Endpoint positions or tangents add constraints and create a different problem. The same care with assumptions governs Willmore normalization and the distinction between immersions and embeddings. The source dates support continuity from 2023 Berry and affine questions through the 2024 geometric forms to the 2026 exact transport and reduction examples. The present proofs unify those dated topics without attributing new historical arguments. The open frontier is the construction of declared higher-dimensional metrics, transports and quotient data with quantitative verification.
chapters.open_frontier: Construct genuine two-dimensional transport refinements, verify regular quotient hypotheses and solve geometric variational problems with the full intended boundary conditions; distinguish representation singularities from failure of the underlying structure.

chapters.title: Analysis, transforms and special functions
chapters.organizing_question: What analytic representation makes the desired quantity computable without losing its domain, norm or normalization?
core_objects: holomorphic functions and positive spectral functions
chapters.overview:
This domain organizes the part of the archive concerned with representing an object so that a question about it becomes a controlled calculation. The representation may be a coefficient sequence, a contour integral, a special-function identity or a spectral measure. In every case, the first task is to state what is being represented and in which space. Bessel’s inequality sees an orthogonal projection; Parseval requires completeness. An atomic pairing uses cancellation in a particular measure. A Fourier transform needs a normalization, and a sampled FFT describes an interpolant before it describes any unknown continuous function. These distinctions provide constructive working rules, not merely objections to formulas. They show how to calculate the information retained by a representation and the error introduced by discarding the rest.

The first family develops that rule through transforms, frames and cancellation. Its four-coordinate Haar calculation accounts exactly for all energy and for the residual after discarding fine detail. A lower frame bound then converts a measurement discrepancy into a state discrepancy with an explicit constant. This is the analytical bridge to reconstruction, while the possibility of a nullspace explains why coefficient summaries can fail to identify an object. Weighted atoms and local Hardy–BMO estimates keep the same measure in the cancellation and pairing; directional image differences explain why a transform may be useful for an edge geometry without being a complete representation.

The second family puts local analytic certificates next to the global information they need. Cauchy extraction requires a holomorphic neighborhood; logarithmic derivatives record zeros or poles with multiplicity; contour counts do not distinguish two simple zeros from one double zero. Positive finite atomic measures give a particularly productive exact class. Their Herglotz functions have simple real poles, a fixed half-plane sign and one simple zero between each pair of poles. The proof uses only explicit signs and derivatives. Branch periods then demonstrate why locally closed differentials can still carry global continuation data.

The third family collects exact integration and special functions by method. Mellin moments, theta and modular reindexing, logarithmic integrals, dilogarithms, elliptic limits and finite trigonometric sums each retain their convergence and branch conditions. The elementary logarithmic moment supplies factorial weights and a rational tail bound for a zeta integral. Its role is to teach a reproducible reduction with a stopping rule, while the original member treatments retain the additional hypotheses needed for their richer constants.

The fourth family treats spectra as data of an operator with a domain and multiplicity. A diagonal model connects a counting function, a heat-trace exponent and a zeta half-plane. It separates fixed-time trace class from a singular short-time limit and shows why changing multiplicity changes dimension. Together, the four families suggest a practical order: fix the representation and its information loss, establish the analytic certificate, calculate with controlled tails, and only then interpret a spectral or geometric invariant. The progression entries identify dated source topics across 2023–2026; they do not date the reconstructed proofs or assert historical discovery priority.
chapters.open_frontier: The main frontier is a portable certificate that carries domains, measures, branches, multiplicities and uniform error bounds through changes of representation. The recovered material does not yet provide one general automated solver.

chapters.title: Differential equations and asymptotics
chapters.organizing_question: How does a stated equation produce a controlled solution, approximation or limiting law?
core_objects: finite asymptotic expansions and sectorial integrals
chapters.overview:
The differential-equation material becomes coherent when the equation, its state space and its boundary or initial data are treated as one object. A familiar profile is not yet a solution, and a formal operator is not yet a closed evolution law. The early hyperbolic-identity discussion is an instructive starting point: substituting a sech-squared wave into the stated KdV normalization forces its amplitude and speed. That same direct method extends to energy laws, diffusion stencils, local Frobenius recurrences and asymptotic remainders. The aim of this chapter is to make each conclusion executable as a sequence of explicit mathematical steps while preserving the assumptions that make those steps valid.

The first family begins with balances. On a periodic circle, the heat equation preserves the mean and decreases the squared fluctuation norm at a rate fixed by the first nonzero Fourier mode. The worked example has only two modes, so its solution and energy derivative can be calculated independently. Nonlinear members then alter the energy or the mobility: a Cahn–Hilliard flow preserves mass while dissipating an energy through a gradient of the chemical potential, whereas an L² gradient flow has a different dissipation law. Coupled diffusion and rotating waves add exchange or flux terms. Boundary conditions and regularity remain part of every calculation.

The second family separates the finite numerical map from its continuum interpretation. The periodic heat stencil has an exact mass identity, a sharp positivity range and an independent Fourier-symbol calculation. Taylor expansion supplies consistency only for sufficiently smooth solutions; stability and defect accumulation are then needed for a finite-time error bound. Distributed communication tests, anisotropy estimates, interpolation and inverse cutoffs are related by this error-budget viewpoint. They are not interchangeable certificates. In particular, the linked cutoff lab balances bias and amplified noise for its own observation model rather than providing a universal PDE solver.

The third family treats local singular equations through normalized bases. A coalescing Euler pair becomes regular after taking a divided difference, and its limiting logarithm has nontrivial unipotent monodromy. The Wronskian distinguishes an actual loss of independence from a bad basis. The recovered Picard–Fuchs examples supply more specific recurrences, while value–derivative matching and gauge conventions determine basis comparison. Extra harmonics in a Hill reduction remain visible instead of being silently renamed Mathieu.

The fourth family makes limiting statements quantitative. Its factorial Borel model has a divergent power series, a valid finite remainder estimate and an explicitly calculable exponential ambiguity. A cubic fold supplies a separate exact three-halves action difference and two-thirds transition scale. The elliptic logarithmic constant and perturbative discriminant questions belong to the same discipline of specified limits, although each uses a different proof. Reading these families in order moves from exact identities to stable approximation, then to local continuation and singular limits. The open task is to make estimates uniform when several of these operations are combined, rather than infer a global theorem from a local germ or a formal expansion.
chapters.open_frontier: Uniform multi-parameter error bounds, resonant basis normalization, nonlinear invariant-preserving schemes and global selection of asymptotic branches remain the central extensions.

chapters.title: Dynamics, mechanics and mathematical modeling
chapters.organizing_question: What state, metric and invariant make a dynamical claim precise and testable?
chapters.overview:
The dynamics material is organized around four choices that a model must make explicit: its state, its clock, its metric and its observations. The same eigenvalues can coexist with very different transient gains; the same geometric path can have different time parametrizations; the same observation can come from different hidden states. The archive’s strongest recurrent ideas are constructive ways to resolve these ambiguities. They include exact Lyapunov matrices, explicit period-two branches, conserved Hamiltonians, dimensionally complete mass balances and derived memory kernels. Each answers a particular question. Their connections become useful once the question and the retained state are stated before the calculation.

The stability family leads with an exact triangular matrix. Its eigenvalues are stable, its Euclidean norm can initially grow, and a positive matrix certifies decay in another norm. This gives a complete example of nonnormal amplification rather than a slogan about it. Continuous and discrete Gramians, common storage functions and hybrid dwell-time bounds extend the same reasoning. Switching incurs a logarithmic metric cost, so stability of the individual modes alone does not establish stability of every switching sequence. A two-line projection calculation supplies a further geometric model: the cycle contraction and the commutator norm are different functions of the same angle. The linked projection lab keeps that distinction visible.

The bifurcation family follows invariant branches and their multipliers. Exact logistic algebra proves the first fixed-point threshold, the born two-cycle and the next flip boundary. That substantial result is deliberately separated from the deeper infinite-cascade and universality questions. Return-map jets identify the cubic term left after a multiplier-minus-one map is composed with itself. Square-root cycle branches and the tanh pitchfork provide further local mechanisms with explicit conditions. None of these local facts alone identifies a global chaotic attractor or establishes a physical renormalization equivalence.

The mechanics and modeling family starts from conservation and units. Hamilton’s equations preserve a stated energy, and a simple turn gives different exponents for elapsed time and action because those quantities integrate reciprocal momentum and momentum respectively. Scalar RG coordinates preserve a fixed-point derivative under an invertible state-coordinate change with the same time variable; a time rescaling changes the rate. Population recurrences, radiation fluxes, drag, chemical yield and volume-to-mass calculations are organized by similarly explicit balance laws. Dimensional agreement narrows a model but does not supply its missing measurements or dimensionless coefficient.

The memory family finally asks whether a reduced state determines its future. Eliminating a hidden linear coordinate produces both a convolution kernel and a source from the hidden initial condition. Omitting them changes the equation. Mechanical words, substitutions and relative periodicity pose discrete versions of the retained-information question. A balanced aperiodic rotation coding can be completely deterministic and have an exact frequency, so irregular appearance is not a chaos certificate. Across these four families, the dated progression traces changing source topics from 2023 onward; the present proofs and worked models are a new organization of that material, with their scope stated independently of historical attribution.
chapters.open_frontier: The most useful next step is to combine certified basins, physically meaningful transient norms and minimal sufficient reduced states for specific models, with quantitative memory-approximation bounds.

chapters.title: Probability and stochastic processes
chapters.organizing_question: What is the complete law, and which operations preserve or transform the uncertainty needed by the question?
chapters.overview:
The probability material is organized by mathematical operation rather than by a single chronological narrative. A model first specifies its sample space and law. Expectations then integrate against that law, dependence connects its coordinates, transitions evolve it in time, and limit theorems approximate it under explicit scalings. This order makes the archive readable without making every probabilistic topic an instance of one favored physical metaphor. The four families progress from compatible outcomes to combinatorial randomness, from processes to asymptotic simplification.

The first family supplies the indispensable foundation. Marginal event probabilities determine an expected count but usually leave the probability of complete success unresolved. Population weights enter an expected square through square roots in its Euclidean representation; amplitude attenuation is a different operation. Posterior predictive dependence gives a second mechanism: future outcomes independent conditional on a latent parameter become dependent after it is integrated out. These exact finite distinctions continue through the three-item surplus model at the end of the source period. Their significance is constructive: the revised question can ask for the range over all admissible couplings instead of assuming an unprovided independence law.

Random sampling and filtrations move the same discipline into combinatorics and topology. Weighted fixed-cardinality samples are normalized by elementary symmetric polynomials, and inclusion probabilities yield expected Euler characteristic by linearity. A random barcode needs more: the actual birth rule and boundary ranks. The four-cycle fixture makes one complete persistence distribution accessible, while the general weighted formula remains an explicit mathematical recipe. This is an important boundary between a finite worked lab and a universal persistent-homology tool.

Stochastic dynamics specify how the law changes. A generator determines expectation evolution, while Itô's second derivative produces an extra term invisible to deterministic differentiation. The OU process provides exact solutions, stationary variances and a transparent comparison with Euler–Maruyama. Linear SDE propagation separates present posterior uncertainty from fresh process noise. Sensor choices are meaningful only when compared against one prior, one target and one terminal horizon. A driver sensor can beat a direct present-target sensor for predicting a future target without violating any monotonicity theorem.

The final family studies simplification under scaling. Finite variance yields the Gaussian averaging fixed point; Cauchy stability shows why that conclusion cannot be universal. Logarithms turn random products into sums with their own transform threshold. Trace-summable Gaussian covariances permit genuine Hilbert-space samples, whereas finite-dimensional consistency alone permits only cylindrical data. Direct couplings give a different approximation method, bounding Lipschitz observables without a central limit theorem. Across all four families, exact finite identities, limiting laws, numerical approximations and empirical calibration remain distinct claims. The atlas executes representative model checks and labels the broader extensions as recipes.
chapters.core_objects: Finite laws and couplings; moments and characteristic functions; weighted subset measures; random filtrations; Markov generators; Wiener integrals; Gaussian covariance operators.
chapters.open_frontier: Combine exact finite combinatorial expectations with quantitative approximation of stochastic dynamics, retaining explicit dependence, topology and error metrics rather than replacing them by one scalar uncertainty score.

chapters.title: Information, statistics and inference
chapters.organizing_question: What does the available observation distinguish, and what claim does its evidence actually justify?
chapters.overview:
Information and inference begin with an observation map and a target. The map decides which states can be distinguished; the target and loss decide whether those distinctions matter. A sampling law then determines which statistical guarantees are available. This domain therefore organizes covariance, entropy, diagnostics and validation around a sequence of questions: what remains hidden, what transformation loses information, what a finite sample can establish, and what a summary preserves. These questions connect closely but their answers are not interchangeable.

Covariance geometry is the first layer. A covariance is a positive semidefinite quadratic form when second moments exist. Null directions record exact linear dependence, and positive averaging preserves the covariance cone. Nonlinear maps add a decisive qualification: a vanishing Jacobian can conceal a nonzero leading uncertainty at the next order. The squared-Gaussian example is fully calculable. It then becomes a hidden-target model, where observing one coordinate perfectly still leaves a squared hidden coordinate random. Conditional expectation gives the optimal estimator and an exact orthogonal decomposition of risk. This identifies separately the part due to structural invisibility and the part due to measurement noise.

Entropy and information geometry describe how laws compare. Relative entropy contracts under a specified stochastic channel; Shannon entropy increases under doubly stochastic mixing but can decrease on approach to a concentrated equilibrium. Mutual information is statistical dependence, not a causal arrow. In parameter space, local KL expansion produces the Fisher quadratic form, with a null direction for common softmax logits. These results explain what may be monitored during optimization while preserving the need to evaluate actual prediction loss independently. Matrix entropy has related exact identities, but the quantum algebra and positivity hypotheses remain visible.

Statistical inference adds sampling and selection. Identifiability is a statement about whether parameters produce distinct observation laws at the stated design. Calibration is a statement about a test statistic under a null. Generalization is a statement about unseen draws. A nested fit automatically improves training residuals, and a prescribed spectrum can always be embedded in a matrix; neither fact proves prediction. Finite uniform bounds and PAC–Bayes methods supply genuine guarantees under declared bounded-loss sampling models. Exact paired randomization supplies another route when the sign-exchangeability null is justified. Its finite p-value remains separate from effect magnitude and practical benefit.

The final family treats the capacity and limitations of summaries. Lossless reconstruction requires an injective encoding and therefore a counting lower bound. Prefix entropy grows by conditional information, independently of a chosen symbolic metric. Spectral flatness, circular concentration, AUROC and pooled correlation each retain particular features and discard others. Their precise invariances are useful; promoting one to a universal certificate is not. The resulting interactive direction is a panel of observation fibres, conditional-risk calculations and finite diagnostic populations. The current atlas supplies small verified fixtures and cross-links to observability and exact-counting labs, while general statistical estimation and historical empirical validation remain unclaimed.
chapters.core_objects: Observation sigma-algebras; conditional expectation and Bayes risk; PSD covariance; KL divergence and channels; Fisher matrices; iid validation laws; randomization populations; finite encodings and diagnostic invariants.
chapters.open_frontier: Design observations sufficient for a specified target or action, then combine exact structural guarantees with independent finite-sample calibration without conflating identifiability, uncertainty and predictive performance.

chapters.title: Optimization and decision theory
chapters.organizing_question: Which objective, feasible set and certificate turn a proposed choice into a justified global decision?
chapters.overview:
Optimization unifies much of the archive only after its inputs are typed. An objective assigns preference, a feasible set defines admissible alternatives, and a certificate supplies a bound valid over all of them. Algorithms search for candidates but do not replace these definitions. This domain is arranged from global convex certificates through constructive updates and finite search to robust decisions under shared uncertainty. It connects the practical question of choosing an action with the mathematical question of which uncertainties can change that action.

Convex duality supplies the cleanest starting point. A feasible primal point and a feasible dual bound can prove global optimality when their values agree. The constrained covariance quadratic makes nullspaces central: a feasible zero-energy null vector changes the answer completely, while a budget orthogonal to the nullspace leads to a pseudoinverse formula. Fenchel conjugates expose the effect of domains and nonsmooth penalties. An SDP zero-gap pair provides a finite exact certificate even when an iterative solver's convergence is irrelevant. In contrast, a stationary cubic equation or an indefinite quadratic requires a separate global analysis.

Proximal and projected methods turn an objective into a reproducible update. Soft thresholding, radial shrinkage and ridge scaling differ because their regularizers differ. The projection variational inequality and smooth descent lemma give a direct finite-step bound. A resolvent step damps curvature according to its eigenvalues and needs a positive quadratic model. Graph heat flow makes the distinction between continuous dissipation and discrete stability explicit. Metric projections, subspace restrictions and Wasserstein pushforwards add useful geometry while preserving their own feasibility and contraction hypotheses. These ideas explain why clipping a gradient, projecting a state and constraining a trajectory are different operations.

Objective design and finite search then expose the combinatorial side. The total-scatter identity can collapse seemingly independent clustering weights into the same objective. Capacity constraints and weighted preferences require different formulations. Pareto nondominance contains legitimate alternatives that no positive linear selector can choose. Exact QUBO enumeration and min-plus transfer provide finite certificates of a chosen problem. Frontier and equivalence-class compression are valid when they preserve complete continuation behavior, not merely a current best answer. Search error, physical-model error and measurement error consequently remain separate parts of an implementation claim.

The final family asks for the cheapest information that settles a decision. When two scores share nuisance uncertainty, subtract them at the same state before optimizing. Their joint difference can have a strict positive lower bound even when separately computed intervals overlap widely. Measurements restrict the compatible-state set, and a finite experiment tree can stop when each remaining fibre certifies one action. The implemented L08 model makes this cancellation visible without claiming a general optimizer or empirical forecast. This endpoint joins the other domains: exact counting can enumerate alternatives, observability can expose decisive fibres, covariance can describe noise, and duality can certify a robust margin. The result is an organized program of mathematical choices whose guarantees state their actual scope.
chapters.core_objects: Convex objectives and conjugates; affine constraints and PSD cones; primal-dual gaps; proximal maps and variational inequalities; finite Pareto sets; frontier signatures; common uncertainty sets and robust margins.
chapters.open_frontier: Construct exact positivity and dual certificates for nonlinear decision differences, then optimize finite measurement trees whose outcome fibres preserve those certificates at minimum guaranteed cost.

chapters.title: Combinatorics and graph mathematics
chapters.organizing_question: What exact information must be retained to count, distinguish or compose finite structures?
chapters.open_frontier: Recover original large-instance tables and proof dependencies; characterize the distinguishing strength of bounded-height graph observations; build minimal boundary quotients that preserve counts as well as values.
chapters.overview:
This domain supplies exact finite objects on which the atlas’s more abstract ideas can be tested. Its organizing operation is a disjoint decomposition: remove the largest tableau entry, choose the next binary project coordinate, separate a graph along a boundary or decompose a path flow. Such a decomposition is useful only if its pieces represent the declared original objects exactly once. Generating products and completion recurrences make those multiplicities explicit. The resulting counts then support a stronger interface: reversible addresses, exact sampling, conditional populations and a unique optimum proved by a singleton threshold census. This is why population definitions and skipped-coordinate factors belong in the mathematics rather than being deferred to implementation.

Graphs contribute a complementary lesson about observations. An adjacency matrix contains more than its eigenvalues, and a full heat operator contains more than its trace or diagonal. The 2023 rook–Shrikhande collision demonstrates an exact loss of structure. The 2026 seven-vertex pair refines the issue: the entire binary size-cut census agrees, while one integer-height coefficient separates the graphs. This is a model for constructive research throughout the report. First prove the collision at the weaker observation; then identify a richer observable and calculate a finite separating witness. It gives a defensible improvement without claiming that the stronger invariant solves every graph-isomorphism problem.

Incidence matrices link this graph thread to topology and optimization. Their rank yields cycle dimension, and spanning forests produce explicit integer cycle bases. The finite DAG path-difference theorem explains which conservation directions can be expressed as differences of admissible routes. Directed acyclicity does not remove undirected circulation: the diamond is the smallest useful reminder. At the optimization boundary, a matching witnesses a necessary number of vertex calls and a cover supplies a sufficient number. The two meet in a complete proof only after the permitted action is fixed. Unrecovered historical call rules and extremal point lists therefore remain concrete retrieval obligations.

The final family turns these principles into composition. Sum–product and min–plus elimination preserve different semiring values through distributivity. A compact separator stores exactly the interaction that future factors can observe. Erasing a physical lane or adding an auxiliary gate is safe only under a corresponding fibre theorem. Equal optimum values can coexist with unequal counting measures, as the 43,680 physical channel assignments and 256 bank tuples show. The interactive capacities follow directly: L02 exposes counts and addresses, L03 inspects a complete graph-invariant collision, and L09 computes boundaries and homology on small declared complexes. These are bounded, inspectable mathematical models. The general elimination, large Petersen optimization and unrecovered routing benchmarks remain recipes or source claims until their actual instances and complete certificates are supplied.

chapters.title: Logic, computation and exact certification
chapters.organizing_question: Which semantics and finite witnesses justify a global computational claim?
core_objects: Action alphabets and deterministic transition systems
Hankel matrices and semiring response tables
chapters.open_frontier: Formalize supplied exact certificates without losing their input semantics; recover operational tables and missing completeness proofs; quantify approximate state reduction separately from exact equivalence.
chapters.overview:
The computation domain joins three questions that must remain distinct: what behavior a machine is intended to preserve, what smaller representation reproduces it, and what certificate establishes that conclusion. The observable state is relative to a declared action alphabet. Present outputs do not determine it. Future equivalence compares outputs after every allowed continuation, and the finite refinement theorem makes that infinite-looking condition executable on a supplied finite transition table. Additive costs enlarge the semantics and must descend with transitions. This explains why a state quotient can be exact for one observer and fail when a reset, query or pinned physical identity is added.

Linear realization gives the parallel quantitative theory of memory. An intertwining identity proves that a smaller state reproduces every time step, while a nonzero Hankel minor proves that no still smaller linear state suffices. The distinction between the reachable subspace and the invisible subspace matters: their intersection quotient determines zero-initial driven order. A recurrence for one observed trajectory, a universal scalar observation recurrence and a multi-output state dimension are different mathematical objects. The min–plus two-by-two gap illustrates the same upper-bound/lower-bound strategy in another algebra, with its scope explicitly limited to additive register factorization.

The certificate family supplies a common proof interface across the archive. Truth tables require a finite domain; quantifiers specify whether a witness is uniform; a polynomial function and a formal polynomial need not coincide; a feasible point is not an optimum; an exact witness is not a complete census. A small checker can validate useful discoveries made by an untrusted search procedure, but its conclusion depends on its declared certificate type. A Bézout identity, a rank factorization and a primal–dual pair establish different propositions. Historical proof diagrams, public recursion identities and two-prime checks retain their narrower meanings unless the missing completeness or dependency arguments are supplied.

The raw-generator theorem is a substantial instance where those obligations are actually met. The annual 2026 bundle contains all 126 integer lattice bases and exact determinant and inverse-column checks. They exclude every collision for any five known positions among nine raw steps, not merely the fixture states. A puncturing argument then proves exact distance n−4 and length-optimal one- and two-word correction. The decoder fixtures separately exercise the implementation. Accepted/rejected sequences have unknown hidden step counts and remain outside that theorem. This distinction should not obscure the genuine strength of the raw certificate.

The atlas’s interactive interface reflects this proof architecture. L01 makes a fixed linear quotient test and cheapest static probe panels inspectable; the finite-machine refinement and adaptive policies are checked recipes. L02 exposes a complete small census and address selection, while its completion-count and inverse-ranking theorems are proved separately. The broader exact certificates remain replayable source computations and mathematical recipes, rather than a claimed general theorem prover or universal SMT replacement. Their unification is a disciplined route from behavior to reduction to proof, with every change of model or quantifier visible.

chapters.title: Control, observability and inverse problems
chapters.organizing_question: What can be recovered or controlled from declared observations, at what cost and with what guarantee?
chapters.open_frontier: Extend finite fibre certificates to supplied nonlinear or noisy models; derive robust experiment policies with computable lower bounds; select regularization from data without unproved source assumptions.
chapters.overview:
The central object in this domain is a requested target seen through an observation. Full-state reconstruction is only one possible target and often demands unnecessary measurements. In finite dimensions, exact target recovery is equivalent to a kernel inclusion and a factorization G=LH. The minimum recovery norm quantifies the amplification of bounded measurement error. A violating invisible vector is an equally useful certificate: it proves that two states have the same data and different targets. The late WIND and observation-geometry topics sharpen this perspective, while the earlier recurrence questions already show its algebraic roots.

Present recovery, prediction and nonlinear identifiability are successive obligations. A present factorization does not make the observation a closed dynamical state; HA=TH additionally requires the invisible kernel to be invariant. Moving observation coordinates acquire B′. A vanishing hidden directional derivative at one point does not establish target constancy on an entire nonlinear fibre. Counting the coefficients of a local wind ansatz does not guarantee a full-rank beam design. These distinctions organize practical sensing questions into exact mathematical tasks instead of letting one rank statistic carry all of their meaning.

Control introduces the dual constructive problem: choose inputs that change the state or target with a certified cost. Gramians characterize finite-horizon reachability and observability without assuming asymptotic stability. Lyapunov identities establish decay in a compatible metric, including nonnormal examples whose Euclidean energy grows transiently. Completion of squares gives full scalar Riccati value proofs with terminal conditions. Descriptor pencils show why the actual constrained model matters: singular E can encode a regular problem, while adding εI can create an unstable artificial mode. These examples make matrix identities useful certificates of behavior, not merely computational diagnostics.

Inverse problems replace exact inversion by controlled approximation. The diagonal models expose the bias-noise split and matching indistinguishable-pair lower bounds. Polynomially decaying singular values give a power rate; exponentially decaying values require a logarithmic rate and an explicit safety margin. Tikhonov’s parameter and Landweber’s stopping time are two ways to choose the same compromise. The guarantee always names a source class and noise model. Neither a tiny residual nor a leading-order cutoff equivalence supplies those assumptions.

Finally, the experiment-design family asks what information should be purchased next. A finite Bellman theorem gives a policy and its matching worst-case lower bound when tests are deterministic and targets explicit. Correlated ellipsoids and hidden conditional variation explain why some extra observations are useful while repeated deficient directions remain irrelevant. L01 combines a fixed linear quotient test with cheapest static probe panels, L04 explores cutoff envelopes, and L08 retains shared uncertainty in robust decisions. These labs demonstrate exact bounded capacities. General nonlinear reconstruction, continuous noisy adaptive design and historical sensor-performance claims require their own supplied models, data and validation arguments.

chapters.title: Quantum, deformation and integrable structures: finite models with explicit boundaries
chapters.organizing_question: Which state, product, coherence equation or spectral model is actually implemented, and what finite certificate proves its claimed behaviour?
chapters.overview:
This domain brings together quantum states and channels, finite noncommutative systems, deformation quantization, braid and fusion data, integrability and formal obstruction theory. Their common feature is that an appealing symbolic relation becomes useful only after its model class and normalization are fixed. The six families supply explicit finite examples and derive their identities, while distinguishing mathematical structure from physical realization, asymptotic convergence and general classification.

Quantum states make the atlas-wide observation problem especially concrete. The Bell state and its dephased mixture agree on all diagonal observations and both one-qubit marginals, but an off-diagonal correlation separates them. This gives a complete finite collision and a constructive additional measurement. Kraus formulas then supply the correct transformation standard: complete positivity is preserved with arbitrary ancillas, and the completeness equation preserves total probability. Instruments retain every measurement branch, so a conditional normalized success state cannot conceal its success probability. Error correction similarly depends on the specified error list, as the repetition code's exact bit-flip correction coexists with quantum distance one.

Finite Weyl systems identify what can hold exactly in finite dimension. Trace forbids the canonical additive commutator, and determinants force a multiplicative commutation phase to be a root of unity. Clock and shift matrices then generate a full finite matrix algebra. Binary symplectic kernels compute Pauli symmetries, while finite quadratic forms and Gauss sums retain the central phase in a projective modular relation. These calculations distinguish finite rational models from irrational operator algebras and distinguish alternating commutation forms from symmetric quadratic polarizations.

Polynomial Moyal calculus supplies the most direct implemented interaction. Its formal star product has exact finite falling-factorial coefficients for monomials. Degree bounds determine which odd corrections can survive, so the exact degree-four family and a genuine fifth-order obstruction are compatible. The new bounded sextic monomial atlas exhausts a declared 784-pair universe and exposes four cases missed by the cubic test. Its complete bounded scope is valuable precisely because general polynomial cancellations and unbounded higher degree remain separate questions.

Braid and fusion examples then make coherence visible. An algebraic Hecke matrix needs no unitarity, a fusion ring needs no associator, and an associator needs pentagon and hexagon equations. The four-object pointed model provides complete finite data and proofs, while Temperley–Lieb Gram forms test positivity independently. Integrable models provide another bridge between descriptions: a finite XXX matrix agrees with regular Bethe roots when the infinite-root state is included, and a two-site Gaudin eigenvector matches a scalar differential potential. KdV tau-functions illustrate nonlinear interaction through a verified exponential coefficient identity.

Finally, obstruction theory explains why first-order success is insufficient. A characteristic-two character cannot lift, a free rank-two family has jumping Hochschild cohomology and an order-twelve equation can fail at order thirteen. These are exact worked models, not negative verdicts about unrecovered larger objects. The domain's interactive capacities are therefore bounded and auditable: compute, classify within a stated finite universe, inspect a witness and identify the next unresolved equation.
core_objects: Density matrices, effects, Kraus maps and instruments
Clock–shift operators and binary symplectic supports
Fusion labels and F/R/S coherence data
Formal parameter rings and obstruction equations
chapters.open_frontier: Extend the bounded monomial Moyal classification to arbitrary polynomial coefficient varieties; recover full anyon and monodromy matrices; prove all-order or completeness statements only with their actual obstruction or spectral data.

families.title: Arithmetic types, completions and certified p-adic precision
families.central_question: Which arithmetic statements survive a change of scalar domain, and what can a finite p-adic calculation actually certify?
families.synopsis: An arithmetic expression includes its scalar ring, topology and precision. The rational field, a p-adic completion, a residue ring and a formal power-series ring support different operations. A unital homomorphism between characteristic zero and characteristic p would send the nonzero integer p both to an invertible element and to zero, an immediate obstruction when the source is a field. Completion instead preserves rational identities while changing which sequences converge. These distinctions turn the early request to separate meanings of Q into a practical specification for every later lifting algorithm. The useful output is a compatible sequence of exact congruences accompanied by derivative and residual valuations. Such a sequence proves an existence statement only with a convergence argument; a zero residue at one precision cannot certify an exact zero. Perfectoid and prismatic language extends this discipline, but carries additional structural hypotheses rather than merely renaming small errors.
definitions: For nonzero rational x, v_p(x) is its prime-p exponent and |x|_p=p^(−v_p(x)); Q_p is the metric completion and Z_p its unit ball.
A simple root modulo p is an integer a with f(a)≡0 mod p and f′(a) not divisible by p. A precision-N representative specifies a coset modulo p^N.
For a nonzero integral series F=Σa_nT^n, μ(F)=min v_p(a_n), and λ(F) is the first index attaining that minimum. Infinite tails must be controlled before certifying these minima.

theorem.statement: If f∈Z_p[X] and a_n is a root modulo p^n with unit derivative, there is exactly one a_(n+1)=a_n+t p^n modulo p^(n+1) reducing to a_n. The compatible sequence converges to the unique root of f in a_1+pZ_p.
theorem.proof: Taylor expansion modulo p^(n+1) gives f(a_n+t p^n)≡f(a_n)+t p^n f′(a_n), since all terms of order two are divisible by p^(2n). Dividing by p^n gives one linear equation for t modulo p. The derivative is a unit, so t is unique. Successive representatives differ by an element of p^nZ_p and hence form a Cauchy sequence. Completeness supplies a limit a; continuity of polynomial evaluation gives f(a)=0. If b is a second root in the same residue class, factor f(a)−f(b)=(a−b)g(a,b). The reduction of g is the nonzero derivative at a_1, so g is a unit and a=b. Newton's update a−f(a)/f′(a) accelerates the same argument: an initial residual valuation at least n becomes at least 2n when the derivative is a unit. An exact vanishing claim requires this theorem or a separate identity, whereas finite arithmetic alone establishes only congruences.

worked_example.setup: Lift the residue 3 of X²−2 modulo 7, then compare a filtered Frobenius residual at two precisions.
worked_example.calculation: At modulus 7, 3²−2=7 and f′(3)=6 is a unit. Writing a_2=3+7t gives 1+6t≡0 mod 7, hence t=1 and a_2=10. Then f(10)=98=2·49; 2+20t≡0 mod 7 gives t=2, so a_3=108 and 108²−2=34·343. Separately, for φ=diag(1,5), Fil¹=span(e₂), the integral quotient residual R(x,y)=π((5φ−I)(x,y)) is 4x. At (25,1) it is 100: invisible modulo 25, nonzero modulo 125. This second calculation certifies failure of exact membership once sufficient precision is supplied.
worked_example.meaning: The root computation supplies certified digits of a genuine 7-adic algebraic number; the residual example explains why a temporary zero display cannot replace a proof.

progression.narrative: The 2023 treatments supply the scalar distinctions and simple-root lifting foundation; this synthesis uses their explicit hypotheses rather than attributing a later precision calculus to the original exchanges.
Perfectoid fields and prisms introduce completeness, Frobenius and structured pairs. Their appearance broadens the objects, while the elementary lifting theorem remains a separate local result.

Filtered Frobenius and power-series invariants expose the distinction between a finite residue and an exact infinite object. Newton lifting gives a positive certificate when its derivative assumptions hold.

The later completion and quintic examples return to concrete compatible lifts. Their exact residue-and-derivative checks support a reusable verification contract, without claiming global factorization or rational roots.

connections.mathematical_bridge: A verifier checks f(a_N)≡0 mod p^N and invertibility of f′(a_N), while the written convergence proof upgrades the certificate to existence.
connections.scope: Finite checking and the infinite theorem have distinct responsibilities.

connections.mathematical_bridge: A crystalline or filtered calculation must name its base, lattice and filtration before a p-adic residual is meaningful.
connections.scope: The elementary residual example is not a proof of a general p-adic Hodge comparison theorem.

interactive_contract.inputs: Prime p, integer polynomial f, initial residue, requested precision N; optional exact filtered matrices.
interactive_contract.outputs: A table of compatible roots, derivative-unit checks and residual valuations; a precision-aware membership verdict.
interactive_contract.validation: Replay each modular root and reduction step exactly; distinguish zero modulo p^N from an identically zero obstruction.
interactive_contract.status: Mathematical recipe; no general solver implemented

families.limits: Simple-root lifting does not cover a vanishing derivative without stronger hypotheses. Truncated series cannot reveal unseen unit coefficients. Perfectoid and prismatic constructions require their full structural definitions; a numerical resemblance to a weight or height supplies none of them.
open_questions: For a singular residue, what extra valuation inequalities guarantee a lift, and can an exact counterexample show why the simple-root contract fails?
Can a proposed filtered calculation provide a certified lower bound on input precision sufficient to distinguish nonvanishing from an unresolved zero residue?

families.title: Divisor incidence, valuations and constructive integer parametrization
families.central_question: How can multiplicative arithmetic become a finite lattice calculation with a complete certificate?
families.synopsis: Prime factorization converts multiplication into addition of exponent vectors. Divisibility becomes a coordinate order, gcd and lcm become coordinate minimum and maximum, and a monomial equation becomes an integer linear system at every prime. This does more than simplify computation: it states exactly which sign cases, valuation bounds and prime supports a complete answer must cover. Divisor incidence then transports scalar arithmetic identities into matrix factorizations. The same identity n=Σ_(d|n)φ(d) controls a positive gcd kernel, its determinant, and a sieve implementation. Thus arithmetic, combinatorics and finite-dimensional energy geometry meet through a declared transform, not merely because they share the word prime. The family includes factorial valuations and prime-stripped block products: one computes the p-power removed, the other computes the remaining unit, and their recombination reconstructs the original factorial exactly.
definitions: For n=∏p_i^a_i, a divisor corresponds to exponents 0≤b_i≤a_i. Its divisor lattice is the product of chains C_(a_i+1).
Dirichlet convolution is (f*g)(n)=Σ_(d|n)f(d)g(n/d). The incidence matrix E has E_(i,d)=1 when d divides i, and zero otherwise.
Legendre’s formula gives v_p(n!)=Σ_(j≥1)⌊n/p^j⌋. The stripped unit U_p(n)=n!/p^v_p(n!) is an integer not divisible by p.

theorem.statement: For G_(i,j)=gcd(i,j), 1≤i,j≤N, one has G=E diag(φ(1),…,φ(N))Eᵀ. Consequently G is positive definite and det G=∏_(d=1)^Nφ(d). Moreover positive solutions of x²y³=2²⁰3¹² are exactly x=2^(10−3r)3^(6−3s), y=2^(2r)3^(2s), with 0≤r≤3 and 0≤s≤2.
theorem.proof: The (i,j) entry of the displayed matrix product is Σ_(d|i,d|j)φ(d)=Σ_(d|gcd(i,j))φ(d)=gcd(i,j). The identity Σ_(d|m)φ(d)=m follows by grouping 1,…,m according to gcd with m. E is lower triangular with diagonal one; every φ(d)>0, giving positive definiteness and the determinant. For the monomial equation, a prime outside {2,3} has 2v_p(x)+3v_p(y)=0, forcing both exponents zero. At p=2, nonnegative integral solutions to 2a+3b=20 require b=2r and a=10−3r, with r=0,1,2,3. At p=3 the same argument gives b=2s and a=6−3s, with s=0,1,2. Independent choices prove both existence and completeness of the twelve solutions. A bounded search would show existence of examples but would not establish that no extra prime or exponent pattern occurs.

worked_example.setup: Factor the 4×4 gcd matrix, count a divisor lattice, and recover a stripped factorial.
worked_example.calculation: For N=4 the diagonal weights are (1,1,2,2), so det G=4. The row for i=4 in E is (1,1,0,1), explaining gcd(4,2)=φ(1)+φ(2)=2. For n=72=2³3², the rank polynomial is (1+t+t²+t³)(1+t+t²), whose coefficients are 1,2,3,3,2,1; its value at one is 12 and its degree is five. For 10!, v_3=3+1=4, so U_3(10)=3628800/81=44800. The recursion U_3(10)=(1·2·4·5·7·8·10)U_3(3), with U_3(3)=2, reproduces 44800.
worked_example.meaning: A positive kernel, a complete Diophantine parametrization and an efficient arithmetic block algorithm arise from distinct but compatible uses of divisor structure.

progression.narrative: Exact exponent manipulation is the early foundation. It supplies arithmetic scale control, without implying that later divisor kernels were already formulated.
The exponent-tower treatment makes parse structure explicit. The same expression discipline is needed before converting a multiplicative constraint into an exponent equation.
Divisor convolution and factorial valuations provide the algebraic and computational components separately, each with an exact domain and proof.
Species, lattice order, kernel factorizations and full valuation parametrizations make the shared exponent structure particularly explicit in the later treatments.

connections.mathematical_bridge: The divisor poset is a product of chains; its zeta matrix is E and its Möbius inverse supplies arithmetic inversion.
connections.scope: This finite poset statement does not identify arbitrary compatibility graphs with complete arithmetic solution sets.

connections.mathematical_bridge: G=EWEᵀ with W positive gives an exact quadratic energy and strict convexity on the declared finite coordinates.
connections.scope: Optimization follows from this factorization, not from prime support alone.

connections.mathematical_bridge: Nonnegative valuation bounds prove that enumeration of the exponent rectangle is exhaustive.
connections.scope: Integer sign and zero cases require separate checks when the original equation permits them.
